frame: Ada Pennick is drafting a second letter about the turtles. The Bilbolster is reading it from a rock pool.
text: Dear Editor, Last month, I wrote to object to jet ski hire in Bluster Bay, and many readers have asked me why I am so certain that jet skis are hurting the turtles. It is a fair question. The northern end of the bay has been a nesting beach for green turtles for as long as anyone can remember, and every summer, volunteers like me count the nests, fence them off and watch the hatchlings scramble down to the water. Until this year, injured turtles were rare. Each nest holds around a hundred eggs, and the hatchlings come out at night, guided by the moonlight on the water. Jet skis are allowed in the bay from 7 am to 7 pm, seven days a week, and the hire shop has twelve of them. On a busy Saturday, all twelve are out on the water at once. I am not against fun, and I am not against tourists, who bring welcome money to our town. But I believe that jet skis are hurting the turtles, and I want to show readers why. I have one sentence left to write before I send this letter, and I want it to be the strongest backing I can give. The council will vote on the jet ski hire licence on 12 December. Yours faithfully, Ada Pennick, turtle volunteer
